I ordered a set of monogrammed handkerchiefs for my grandpa. The monogram was stitched with the wrong initials and the seller blamed me, even though my order confirmation shows the right letters. I'm very upset
The resistance bands snapped after just two weeks of use.  One snapped while I was mid-rep and hit me in the face.  I'm lucky it didn't hit my eye.  Dangerous product
To be fair, the "travel size" umbrella is very travel friendly. It travels straight inside out at the first breath of wind, then travels into the nearest trash can
The hat is listed as size 7 1/4.  Measuring the inner band, it is 21.5 inches, which corresponds to a size 6 7/8.  It does not fit my head, which is 7 1/4.  The sizing is wrong
My bridesmaids' shoes were all supposed to be the same shade of champagne.  Three arrived in a noticeably darker color.  In photos, it looks like they came from different weddings.  Disappointing.

I'll admit these rain boots for work look nice and are easy to slip on. But they crack at the ankle crease within two months of daily wear, and water gets in. On a construction site that's a real problem. Not durable
These heeled sandals have a strap that cuts right across my toes, and after an hour I had red welts.  I couldn't make it through dinner.  I took them off and walked home barefoot
Arrived dirty and broken!

My twins needed new swimsuits for summer camp and these were affordable, which I liked.  But both suits had seams coming apart after the first week of daily swimming, and one of the straps broke.  I'm buying replacements in July.  Not a good deal after all

The sports bra in my size actually exists, which I was thrilled about.  Sadly that's the only thing it has going for it.  The band rolls up, the straps slip off my shoulders, and the support is about the same as a tank top.  Back to searching
The webcam's microphone picks up nothing but static, and the video is so grainy that people on calls asked if I was in a cave. I tried it on two computers. It's just bad.

The swim bag is a good size and the mesh lets things dry out, which I appreciated. But the drawstring cord frayed and broke after a month, and the bottom seam split. My goggles fell out in the parking lot and got run over. Not a great buy

To be balanced: the luggage tags are brightly colored and easy to spot. However:
1. The plastic window fogs so the address can't be read
2. Two of the four straps broke on the first trip
3. The tags are smaller than pictured
They didn't make it to the second trip
The jacket is described as "oversized." I think they meant "over-priced," because the fit is tiny

I've now owned these hiking pants for two months, which I think is long enough for a fair review. I'll start with what I like: the fit is good, the articulated knees give plenty of room when climbing, and the zip-off legs are convenient on hot afternoons.

Unfortunately, the problems outweigh the positives. First, the "quick dry" fabric took over three hours to dry after a light rain, while my old pants are dry in under an hour. Second, the zippers for the zip-off legs are cheap coil zippers that catch on the fabric every time, and the left one has already lost two teeth. Third, the seat has worn noticeably thin from sitting on rocks, which is something hiking pants should be designed for. Finally, the snap on the cargo pocket pulled out of the fabric in week three, taking a chunk of cloth with it. I contacted the company and was told the pants are "lightweight by design." Lightweight is fine. Fragile is not. I won't be buying another pai

I don't usually write reviews but I feel like other plus size women deserve an honest one, because the photos on this listing are misleading.  The model wearing the 3X is clearly not a 3X, the dress is pinned in the back in at least two places, you can see the clips in the mirror in the third photo if you look closely.

When it arrived, I was happy at first.  The fabric is a nice heavy jersey, the color is a deep emerald, and the stitching looks solid.  But the dress is cut completely straight, no shaping at the waist at all, so on a body with curves it hangs from the bust like a tent.  The sleeves are also very tight compared to the rest of the dress.  I tried belting it and it just bunched up.  I tried it with a cardigan and it looked like a nightgown.  I really wanted this to be my go-to dress for work, but I can't wear it anywhere.

I have hesitated to write this review, as I have been a loyal customer of this firm since my first job in 1969, when I bought my first pair of their wingtips with my second paycheck. For forty years they have been the only shoe I have worn to the office.

The pair I received last month looks correct. The leather is still a fine calf and the broguing is as handsome as ever. But the construction is not the same. The soles are now cemented rather than Goodyear welted, which I confirmed with my cobbler, who has resoled my shoes for twenty years. He tells me these cannot be resoled at all. After six weeks the heel is already worn at an angle, and the leather lining has begun to separate at the heel. The shoe is now, in effect, disposable. At the price they still charge, I find this a betrayal of the reputation they built. I will keep my old pairs going as long as my cobbler can manage it

I really wanted this convertible car seat cover and stroller blanket combo to work, because it's such a smart idea and the fleece lining is incredibly soft. My daughter was born in December so I thought it would be perfect for winter.

The problems started almost right away. The elastic edge that's supposed to hold it on the car seat is too loose, so the cover slides down over her face every time I carry the seat. I've had to tuck it in with my hand while walking, which is tricky when you're also carrying a diaper bag. When I use it as a stroller blanket, the clips that are supposed to attach it to the stroller don't fit our stroller's bar, so it slips off and drags on the ground. After a week it was filthy on the bottom and the fleece started pilling after the first wash. I'm now using a regular blanket and a separate car seat cover, which work much better

I bought this MP3 player as a cheaper alternative to the big brand ones and for the first week I was pretty happy. The sound quality is decent through good headphones, the screen is bright, and it has an FM radio, which the big brand ones don't.

Then I started running into problems. The software that comes with it is terrible: it crashes on my computer about half the time, and when it does work it scrambles the song order and drops album art. The battery life is about four hours, not the twelve claimed on the box. The headphone jack became loose within a month, so if I move the cord at all the sound cuts out in the left ear. And last week it froze completely and wouldn't turn on until the battery ran down overnight. I'm going to save up for the brand name one. Sometimes you really do get what you pay for

I ordered this veil four months before my wedding to make sure I had plenty of time, and I'm glad I did. It arrived in a beautiful box and the lace edge is lovely, exactly what I'd hoped for.

However, the moment I tried it on with my dress, it was obvious that the veil was a completely different shade of ivory, almost yellow next to my gown, even though I'd ordered the color matched to my dress designer's ivory. The comb was also sewn on so loosely that it wobbled and wouldn't stay in my hair. I contacted the seller with photos and they suggested I "try it in natural light." I did. It was still yellow. They eventually agreed to an exchange, but the second veil had the same color issue. I ended up buying a veil from my bridal salon at three times the price. I'm grateful I had the time to fix it, but I'd warn other brides to be very careful with this seller

I have three boys and I go through jeans like crazy, so I was excited when I found these "reinforced knee" jeans that promised to stand up to active kids.  The price was a little higher than what I usually pay, but I figured if they lasted it would be worth it.

The first thing I noticed is that they run small, my 8 year old who wears a regular 8 everywhere else needed a 10 in these.  The second thing is that the reinforced knee is just a second layer of thin fabric sewn on the inside, and within three weeks the outer layer had worn through and the inner patch was starting to show.  My middle son's pair ripped right at the seam where the patch is attached.  My oldest's pair has held up the best, but the dark wash has faded to a blotchy gray after maybe ten washes.  I won't be buying them again.  Regular cheap jeans last about as long and cost a lot less.

As someone who runs about 40 miles a week, I'm pretty picky about running shoes, and I was excited to try these because the reviews were so positive.  Out of the box, they felt great.  The cushioning is soft, the upper is breathable, and they're very light.

After about 80 miles, though, the cushioning had already started to feel flat, and by 120 miles the heel foam was visibly compressed and creased.  I usually get 400 miles out of a pair.  The outsole is also wearing down very quickly, especially at the forefoot, where the rubber is already smooth.  And around mile 100, I started getting pain on the outside of my right knee, which I've never had before.  When I switched back to my old shoes, the knee pain went away within a week.  I think these shoes might be fine for someone who runs a few miles a week, but they're not built for serious training

I'm a hospital nurse who works three twelve hour shifts a week, so I need my scrubs to hold up.  These came highly recommended by a coworker, and I'll admit the fit is much more flattering than my old boxy ones.  The fabric has some stretch, which makes bending and lifting easier.

But here's the problem.  After about a month of washing them in hot water, which is what we're required to do to sanitize them, the color faded unevenly.  The tops are now a blotchy gray-blue and the pants are a different shade entirely, so they don't match anymore.  The fabric has also started pilling in the inner thighs and under the arms, and one pocket seam has come open.  For the price, which is almost double what I paid for my old scrubs, I expected them to last at least a year.  I'm going back to the cheaper brand

I spent a long time picking out this bracelet for my wife's 25th anniversary present, because I wanted something special and the product description said it was sterling silver with genuine sapphires.  It came in a lovely velvet box and she cried when she opened it, which made me very happy.

About two weeks later, she noticed the silver was turning dark in spots.  Then one of the "sapphires" fell out, and when she picked it up, it was clearly glass, you could see a tiny bubble in it.  We took the bracelet to a jeweler, who told us it's silver-plated brass and the stones are glass.  I contacted the seller, who claimed the product was exactly as described and refused a refund.  I disputed the charge with my credit card company.  I'm not upset about the money so much as I am that my wife's anniversary gift turned out to be a fake.  Please don't buy from this seller

ok so i don't usually write reviews but i need to warn people. i bought this backpack for college because it was cute and it had a usb charging port on the side, which seemed really cool.

first week was fine. second week the usb cable inside came disconnected and i had to dig through the lining to reattach it. third week the strap started fraying where it connects to the bag. by midterms the bottom of the bag had a hole in the corner and my pens kept falling out. i tried to sew it but the fabric is so thin it just tore more. also the "water resistant" thing is a lie, i got caught in the rain walking to class and my notes got soaked. so yeah. cute bag, cool idea, terrible quality. spent more on this than my last two backpacks combined and it didn't even last a semester

I've been searching for the perfect pair of tall black boots for years, and when I found these I thought my search was over.  They're so sleek and the heel height is perfect for walking around the city.  I wore them to work the day they arrived and got so many compliments.

But within a month, the problems started piling up.  The zipper on the left boot started separating at the bottom, so it slowly unzips as I walk.  The faux leather is creasing and cracking around the ankle, and it's starting to flake off in little pieces.  The heel tip on the right boot came off on the subway stairs and I almost fell.  I took them to a shoe repair shop and the guy basically laughed and told me they weren't worth fixing.  I'm so disappointed.  I really wanted these to be my winter boots for years, not week

Hello, I want to tell my experience with this product because I think it is important for other buyers outside of USA.

I order this winter coat to Norway in October because the price is good and the picture look very warm. The shipping take almost 7 weeks and I pay also big tax for customs, almost 40% of the price. When the coat arrive, the first impression is good, the color is nice and the material look strong.

But when I wear it outside, it is not warm at all. In Norway in December it is minus 15 and I feel cold after only 10 minutes. The description say it is for very cold weather but I think it is only for autumn. Also the hood is very small and does not cover my head with a hat. I cannot return because the shipping is too expensive. Now I must buy another coat. I am very disappointed

Let me tell you a story about the "luxury" cashmere sweater I purchased from this listing.

Chapter one: it arrives, folded beautifully in tissue paper. I am delighted. It is soft. It is gray. It is, for one shining moment, everything I hoped.

Chapter two: I wear it to work. By lunchtime, the elbows have developed tiny pills. By the end of the day, the pills have pills.

Chapter three: I hand wash it in cold water with special wool soap, like a responsible adult. It emerges two sizes smaller and slightly crunchy.

Chapter four: I examine the label more carefully, which I should have done in chapter one. It says "cashmere blend." The blend is 5% cashmere, 95% everything else.

The end. Moral of the story: read the tag

I'M GOING TO TRY TO STAY CALM WRITING THIS. I ORDERED TWO PAIRS OF SHOES FROM THIS SELLER ON AUGUST 12TH. ON AUGUST 30TH, AFTER NOT RECEIVING ANYTHING, I EMAILED THEM. THEY SAID THE SHOES WERE ON BACKORDER. NOBODY HAD TOLD ME. I ASKED TO CANCEL THE ORDER AND THEY SAID IT WAS "TOO LATE TO CANCEL" BECAUSE IT WAS "IN PROCESSING." ON SEPTEMBER 20TH, ONE PAIR ARRIVED, IN THE WRONG SIZE. THE OTHER PAIR NEVER CAME. I SENT THE WRONG PAIR BACK AND IT'S NOW NOVEMBER AND I HAVE NOT RECEIVED A REFUND FOR EITHER PAIR. I HAVE THE TRACKING NUMBER SHOWING THEY RECEIVED MY RETURN. THEY STOPPED ANSWERING MY EMAILS. I'VE FILED A DISPUTE WITH MY CREDIT CARD. I'M WRITING THIS SO NOBODY ELSE HAS TO GO THROUGH THIS.

Some years ago I bought an overcoat of this brand that I still wear on the coldest days. I recently purchased a second coat of the same name and style, expecting a similar garment. It is not similar.

The wool, described as "100% virgin wool," is noticeably thinner and has a flat, lifeless feel. The lining, formerly a heavy twill, is now a slippery polyester that has already torn at the left sleeve. Two of the buttons were loose when the coat arrived, and one came off in my hand when I first fastened it. Perhaps most tellingly, the coat no longer carries the "made in" label of the country where the brand built its name. I returned the coat and wrote to the company, but received only an automated reply. I will continue wearing my old coat and advise others to look elsewhere

I'm writing this because I wish someone had warned me.  This swimsuit is advertised as offering "full support for fuller figures," and it's sold in sizes up to 26W.  I'm a 22W with a 40DD bust, so I thought I was well within their range.

The top has no underwire, no molded cups, and the straps are thin spaghetti straps that dug into my shoulders within minutes.  Full support it is not.  The bottom is cut very high on the leg, so it doesn't cover what it should, and the tummy control panel is just a slightly thicker piece of the same fabric.  After an hour at the beach the fabric had stretched out so much that it was sagging.  I've been to the beach in a lot of swimsuits and this was the most uncomfortable and self-conscious I've ever felt.  I would not recommend it to anyone with curves

I bought this "premium" leather case for my new phone and I regret it.  First, the leather is clearly not leather.  It has a plastic sheen and a chemical smell that hasn't gone away after a month.  Second, the magnetic clasp is so strong that it interfered with my phone's compass, and maps kept telling me I was facing the wrong way.  Third, the card slots inside are so tight that it took me two minutes to get my debit card out at the grocery store, with a line behind me.  Fourth, the case added so much bulk that my phone no longer fits in my car's phone holder.  Finally, after six weeks the edges started peeling and the stitching on the spine came apart.  For the price, it should be the best case on the market.  It's one of the worst I've owned

I'm writing this review because I'm still upset months later. I ordered matching bridesmaid dresses from this seller for my five bridesmaids and myself in a coordinating color, three months before the wedding. The dresses arrived two weeks late, which I could have forgiven.

What I couldn't forgive was that the dresses were not the same color. Two were a deep purple, two were a lighter lavender, and one was almost blue. The fabric also varied: some were a heavy satin and others a thin, shiny polyester. The seller insisted that "dye lots may vary." We didn't have time to reorder, so we had to scramble to buy new dresses from a local shop at the last minute, which cost my bridesmaids a lot of money. The seller refused to refund us because the dresses were "as described." I have pictures of all five dresses side by side. They are not the same dress

I'm usually not one to write long reviews but this product made me so frustrated that I need to warn other parents.  I bought these toddler rain boots because they had good ratings and my son loves the dinosaur design.  They are cute, I'll admit that.

But here's what happened.  The first time he wore them to the park, he jumped in a puddle and came home with soaking wet socks.  I checked and there's a crack in the sole of the left boot, right under the toe.  I thought maybe it was a fluke, so I exchanged them.  The second pair cracked in the same spot within two weeks.  On top of that, the inside of the boots has a hard seam at the back that rubbed his heels raw.  He cried every time I tried to put them on after that.  Two pairs, two failures, and a kid who now refuses to wear rain boots.  Not worth it at any price

I've been doing triathlons for about six years and I bought this wetsuit after my old one finally wore out.  The sizing chart put me in a medium, which is what I've always worn in other brands.

First problem: getting it on took me almost fifteen minutes and a lot of sweating, and once it was on, it was so tight in the shoulders that I could barely lift my arms over my head.  Second problem: in the water, it let in a lot of cold water at the neck, which flushed out any warmth.  Third problem: on my second open water swim, the zipper pull broke off, and I had to have a friend cut me out of the zipper area.  The company said zipper damage isn't covered by the warranty.  I swam a race in a borrowed wetsuit the following weekend.  This one is now a very expensive piece of rubber in my garage

I bought this "organic cotton" baby sleeper set because my daughter has sensitive skin and I wanted something gentle.  The packaging is lovely and the colors are soft pastels.

Within an hour of putting her in the first sleeper, she had red bumps on her neck and arms.  I thought maybe it was something else, so I washed all the sleepers in fragrance-free detergent and tried again a few days later.  Same rash.  I looked more closely at the tags and found that only the outer layer is organic cotton; the inner lining is polyester, and the tag also lists a "finish" that isn't explained anywhere.  Her pediatrician said it was probably a contact reaction.  I've thrown them all out.  The listing should be honest about what these are made of, because parents of babies with sensitive skin are the ones who'll be looking for them.

Having read the glowing reviews, I purchased this travel garment bag for a two-week business trip.  I want to document what happened, so that others can make an informed choice.

Day 1: The bag fits two suits and several shirts as claimed, and folds neatly into a carry-on size.

Day 3: The hook at the top, which holds the hangers, cracked when I hung the bag in my hotel closet.  I improvised with a binder clip.

Day 6: The main zipper began to separate from the bottom up, exposing the suits.

Day 9: The shoulder strap's clip snapped as I walked through the airport, and the bag fell onto the floor.

Day 14: I arrived home with the bag held together with packing tape.

The fabric itself held up well.  Everything else failed.  I would not recommend this bag for any trip longer than an overnight.

I'm genuinely so disappointed with this dress.  I saw it on a few style blogs and it looked absolutely stunning on everyone, so I ordered it in my normal size for a friend's engagement party.

When it arrived, the first thing I noticed was that the fabric is much thinner and shinier than it looks in photos, almost like a costume.  The second thing I noticed was that the hem was uneven, about an inch longer on the left side.  I tried it on anyway and the zipper caught on the fabric halfway up and wouldn't budge.  I spent twenty minutes working it loose and ended up with a small tear near the zipper.  I wore something else to the party.  I've emailed the seller twice asking about a return and haven't heard anything.  Save yourself the stress and buy from a store where you can try things on

I write this review because I want people in other countries to know before buying.  I order the leather bag to Indonesia.  The seller say shipping is 10 to 15 days, but I receive after 45 days.  The box was broken and the bag inside was wet, maybe from rain.

The leather is not real leather, it is plastic, I can see the fabric under it on the edges.  Also the smell is very strong, like chemical, and after two weeks it still smell.  The zipper is not smooth and the handle is very hard.  I write to the seller three times with pictures.  First they say send it back, but the shipping cost is more than the bag.  Then they stop answering.  I lose my money and my time.  Please be careful

I bought this "personalized" leather wallet as a graduation gift for my nephew, and I want to share what happened because I was so let down.

I placed the order three weeks before the graduation and paid extra for rush processing. The wallet arrived the day after the ceremony. The engraving was crooked and the font was not the one I had chosen. The leather also had a deep scratch across the front that looked like it had been there before engraving. When I contacted the seller, they offered me 15% off a future order, which I declined. They refused a refund because the item was "personalized and non-returnable." I gave my nephew a card with cash instead. He's a sweet kid and said it was fine, but I'm still annoyed

I've worked construction for twenty years and I know what a good work boot feels like.  These are advertised as "built for the toughest job sites," with a composite toe and an oil-resistant sole.

I wore them for about six weeks.  In that time, the stitching along the side of the left boot came apart, and water started coming in whenever I stepped in a puddle.  The sole has worn down noticeably at the heel, much faster than any boot I've owned.  The insole is a flat piece of foam that compressed completely in the first week, so I've been standing on what feels like a board all day.  My knees and lower back have been aching more than usual.  I've gone back to my old brand and the pain is already better.  These are not job site boots

i want to warn anyone thinking of buying these 'premium' wireless headphones. i saved up for like two months to get them and i'm honestly so mad.

first the bluetooth drops every few minutes, even when my phone is in my pocket. second the battery lasts like 3 hours not 20. third the ear pads are fake leather and they're already peeling after a month, like little black flakes all over my neck. fourth the left side started making a crackling noise when the volume is up. i tried resetting them like 10 times and contacted customer service, they told me to reset them again. i returned them and got my money back eventually but it took 3 weeks and like 5 emails. not worth it.

I have discovered the world's most advanced umbrella technology, and I'd like to share my findings.

This umbrella has a revolutionary self-inverting feature.  At the slightest breath of wind, it flips itself inside out, presumably to let the rain clean the interior.  It also has an innovative self-disassembly mode: after three uses, one of the ribs detached itself and wandered off.  The handle features an ergonomic wobble that keeps your wrist engaged and alert.  And the canopy uses a breathable fabric that lets a fine mist of rain pass through onto your head, keeping you refreshed.

All jokes aside, it's a terrible umbrella.  It broke in a week and kept me about as dry as a paper bag would.  Spend your money on something else

I SENT THEM THE TRACKING SHOWING IT WAS SIGNED FOR BY SOMEONE AT THEIR WAREHOUSE. THEY THEN SAID IT WAS "RETURNED DAMAGED" AND REFUSED THE REFUND. IT WAS NEVER EVEN TAKEN OUT OF THE BAG.
